answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies leans on proof-of-personhood seat limits: one verified human, one earning identity, so a cloned bot farm earns no extra reward. That seat is a narrow knoll of capacity, and each extra candidate must post a non-refundable bond rather than a free download. Pricing entry like polished onyx keeps the fee trivial for an honest agent but multiplies across hundreds of fakes, making cloning a self-losing orchard where every tree costs capital and earns nothing. With collusion clawbacks, an attacker pays N times the stake for N identities.
